definition: Crew scheduling is the process of assigning crews to operate transportation systems, such as rail lines or airlines..
details: Crew scheduling is the process of assigning crews to operate transportation systems, such as rail lines or airlines.

explainer.lead: Crew scheduling is the task of deciding which workers will operate which trips or services in a transportation system. A good schedule gives every service the crew it needs while making workable assignments for the people involved.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a railway with many trains and a group of drivers. Crew scheduling is like making a fair, workable rota so every train has a driver and nobody is expected to be in two places at once. It helps turn a list of journeys into a plan people can actually carry out.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers model services as duties that require crews, then search for assignments that satisfy coverage and feasibility requirements. The main pitfalls are producing overlapping or otherwise unworkable duties and creating a schedule that is difficult to adjust when operations change.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a set of services S and crews C, choose assignments so that each required service is covered and each crew's assigned sequence is feasible. With binary x_(s,c) indicating whether crew c operates service s, basic coverage can be written as sum_c x_(s,c) = 1 for every s in S, alongside constraints defining feasible crew schedules. Larger instances are difficult because sequencing and feasibility constraints link many assignment decisions.

explainer.example: Suppose a small rail operator has three morning trains—A, B, and C—and two available drivers. If Driver 1 can operate A and then B without an overlap, while Driver 2 operates C, every train is covered and neither driver receives two simultaneous duties.

explainer.intuition: A transportation timetable says what must run; crew scheduling decides who will run it. The challenge is to cover the required work without giving any crew an impossible combination of assignments.
howItWorks: List the transportation services that need crews.
Identify the crews available to take assignments.
Check which services each crew can feasibly operate.
Assign crews so that all required services are covered.
Produce each crew's schedule for use in operations.
explainer.whyItMatters: Without a crew schedule, a transportation timetable is not an operating plan: services may lack crews, or crews may receive assignments they cannot carry out. Scheduling connects planned services with the people needed to run them.
misconceptions: It is not the passenger timetable: the timetable lists services, while crew scheduling assigns people to operate them.
It is not simply filling empty slots; assignments must also form feasible schedules for individual crews.
